headline: Voted not to recommend Noyes and Cypress streets school drop-off ordinance as written; referred it to City Solicitor for review.
summary: The committee heard residents' concerns about a proposed ordinance restricting access on Noyes and Cypress streets during school drop-off and pick-up hours. Members voted unanimously not to recommend the ordinance as written and referred it to the City Solicitor. The committee also made several recommendations on pedestrian signals, crosswalks, and signs.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 15, 2026 meeting by unanimous consent.
Tabled the review of September 2026 city-wide crash data until the November meeting.
Voted unanimously not to recommend the ordinance as written and referred it to the City Solicitor for review of its language, with a request to consider whether an ordinance is the right mechanism.
Passed unanimously a motion to acknowledge concerns and not install a flashing pedestrian light at Rumford and Centre Street until a crosswalk policy and funding source are set.
Recommended that pedestrians crossing Centre Street to reach school use the Centre/N Spring intersection, where a crossing guard is present during walk to school hours.
Passed unanimously a motion to keep concurrent pedestrian phasing at Centre Street and Green Street and to recommend a Leading Pedestrian Interval once the new controller is installed.
Demers agreed to upgrade the faded crosswalk signage at the South Street crosswalk at Wilson Ave.
Agreed a crosswalk on Abbott Road at Loon Ave could be considered in the future with the annual paving program.
Agreed adequate signage is in place and did not recommend an additional sign on Little Pond Road before Auburn Street.
Did not recommend a crosswalk on Bow Street at Rockingham Street.

plain_text:
October 20, 2026 
Page 1 of 5 
 
CITY OF CONCORD 
TRAFFIC OPERATIONS COMMITTEE 
MINUTES OF OCTOBER 20, 2026 
 
The Traffic Operations Committee (TOC) met at 9:00 am on October 20, 2026 
in the Second Floor Conference Room, 41 Green Street 
 
Attendees: Alec Bass, Matthew Casey, Matt Cashman, Kevin Demers, Karen Hill, and Harold 
Palmer 
 
Absent: Fred Reagan, Michael Bezanson 
 
Non-voting Staff: Sarah Ferguson 
 
Guests: Pat DeAngelis (51 Noyes Street) 
Jim McConaha (7 Cypress Street) 
Chris Moore (9 Cypress Street) 
Linda Zollo (15 Noyes St) 
 
1.   Introductions  
 
2.   Approval of Minutes  
 a.  September 15, 2026 TOC Draft Meeting Minutes 
On a motion made by Bass, seconded by Demers, the meeting minutes of 
September 15, 2026 were approved. The motion passed by unanimous consent. 
 
3.   Review City-Wide Crash Data 
 
 a.   September 2026 
Item tabled to the November meeting. 
 
4.   Council/Committee Updates 
None. 
 
5.   Project Updates 
Hill provided a brief update on the status of various ongoing Engineering projects.   
 
6.   Unfinished Business  
 a.  None. 
 
7.   New Business 
 a.  Referral from City Council regarding a proposed ordinance amending the Code of 
Ordinances; Title II, Traffic Code; Chapter 17, Vehicles and Traffic, Article 17-6, 
Miscellaneous Rules, by adding Section 17-6-12, Noyes Street and Cypress Streets - 
Restricted Access During School Drop-Off/Pick-Up Hours; together with a 
communication from John F. Weaver
October 20, 2026 
Page 2 of 5 
 
Hill provided a summary of prior discussions and the status of the City 
Council/TPAC discussions. She confirmed the City Manager sent a letter to Concord 
School District (CSD) but a response has not yet been received. 
 
Linda Zollo, 15 Noyes Street, shared her continued concerns about the School 
District’s plan to add traffic to her neighborhood. She feels that every effort from 
the neighborhood has been refuted or knocked down and the ordinance is the only 
way to maintain the safety of the neighborhood and children walking to and from 
school. She feels as though this is a social justice concern, as not every family is 
able to drop their children off at school and that many have to walk and will be 
walking in this neighborhood. She feels that the safety of the campus itself, and 
the drop-off parents are being prioritized. She mentioned that 79 buses will pass 
her house each day, and her concerns are that a well-established neighborhood 
with mature trees will be impacted with this proposal.  
 
Pat DeAngelis, 51 Noyes Street, discussed the current ordinance restrictions in 
place in the neighborhood. DeAngelis noted existing no-right-turn restrictions from 
Clinton Street intended to discourage cut-through traffic. She has concerns with 
increased traffic mixing with children walking to school. DeAngelis stated that the 
School Board has not presented an alternative plan and that the ordinance appears 
to be the neighborhood’s remaining option. 
 
Chris Moore, 9 Cypress Street, mentioned that he is retired and is home to observe 
the neighborhood. He expressed frustration that residents felt compelled to 
propose an ordinance and hire legal counsel. He mentioned concerns with sight 
lines and turning movements that already exist in the neighborhood. He expressed 
concern about the School Board’s responsiveness to the neighborhood. He invites 
everyone to visit Cypress and Noyes Street to see the actual current traffic 
concerns. He also shared concerns that sidewalks would impact parking. 
 
Jim McConaha, 7 Cypress Street, shared a letter from a neighbor, see attached. He 
shared concerns that the proposed high volume of traffic is not safe. He described 
the neighborhood as historically quiet, with primarily residential traffic and 
pedestrian activity. He expressed concerns about the effects of sidewalks on 
neighborhood character, resubmitted the neighborhood petition, and stated that 
alternatives to the original plan had been rejected. 
 
Hill clarified that the City Manager’s letter addresses the traffic pattern and 
sidewalks, while TOC’s discussion would focus on the referred ordinance. She 
added that the referral was also sent to the City Solicitor’s office and initial 
concerns have been raised about ambiguity, enforceability, and liability. Hill does 
not feel that the ordinance as written is the solution to the concerns.  
 
Casey thanked the residents for sharing their concerns, but expressed concerns 
about enforcing the ordinance as presented.  
 
There was a brief discussion between the Committee and the residents.
October 20, 2026 
Page 3 of 5 
 
Hill moved not to recommend the ordinance as written and to refer it to the City 
Solicitor for further review of its language, seconded by Demers. 
 
Discussion: 
Demers noted that although the City has made ordinance changes to 
accommodate other traffic concerns, such as parking and turning movements, he 
was concerned that similar restrictions could be applied to many neighborhoods 
and schools throughout the City. 
 
Casey and Bass questioned whether an ordinance is the appropriate solution.  
 
Casey proposed amending the motion to request consideration of whether an 
ordinance is the appropriate mechanism to address neighborhood concerns, 
recognizing that the School District’s pending response to the City could identify 
alternatives that affect the need for an ordinance. 
 
Hill made a motion to accept the proposed amendment to her original motion, 
seconded by Demers. 
 
Cashman confirmed the Superintendent received the City’s letter and plans to 
respond. He thanked attendees and encouraged residents and City staff to 
consider the forthcoming response. 
 
Chris Moore stated concern that the School District claims there is no space for 
another alternative, but they have the space for three full-sized soccer fields and 
bleachers. He believes the solution is keeping the buses and vehicles using the 
main entrance and Conant as they always have.  
 
Residents expressed concern that the School District’s traffic engineer had not 
presented an alternative excluding Noyes and Cypress Streets for comparison with 
the current proposal. 
 
All in favor, the motion passed unanimously. 
 
Cashman left the meeting after this discussion.  
    
 b.  Referral from City Council regarding a communication from Casey Callahan, 
resident of Centre Street, requesting consideration of a flashing pedestrian light at 
the intersection of Rumford and Centre Street 
The Committee reviewed the resident’s concern and noted that City records 
showed no recent pedestrian crashes at the intersection. 
 
Hill noted Centre Street’s width and history of speeding concerns and stated that 
improvements such as bump-outs could be considered with future corridor paving. 
 
Bass made a motion to acknowledge the concerns, but until a crosswalk policy, to 
include RRFBs installation and priority locations, and a funding source is
October 20, 2026 
Page 4 of 5 
 
established, it is premature to install them at this location over potential others in 
the City, seconded by Casey, all in favor, the motion passed unanimously. 
 
The Committee agreed that the location should be added to the list for further 
evaluation in the future. 
 
The Committee also recommended that if the pedestrians are crossing Centre 
Street to travel to school, they could cross at the intersection of Centre/N Spring 
where a crossing guard is present during walk to school hours. 
 
 c.  Referral from City Council regarding a communication from Abby Dollries, Ward 4 
resident, requesting consideration be given for an extended Walk Signal Duration 
and an implementation of an Exclusive Pedestrian Phase at the intersections of 
Centre Street and Green Street 
The Committee reviewed the resident’s concern and confirmed concurrent 
pedestrian phasing is very common at traffic signals in the downtown area. Hill 
confirmed the City is converting more as projects move forward to introduce 
consistency.   
 
Hill discussed an upcoming project that will replace the intersection controller, 
which would allow a leading pedestrian interval (LPI) to be introduced, as 
appropriate.  
 
Hill made a motion to retain the concurrent pedestrian phasing at the intersection 
while addressing the concerns raised by recommending the implementation of a 
Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI) once the new controller is installed and 
confirming that appropriate vehicle yield-to-pedestrian signage is in place 
seconded by Palmer, all in favor, the motion passed unanimously.  
 
 d. 
 
 
 Resident request through SeeClickFix in regards to safety concerns at the South 
Street crosswalk at Wilson Ave 
The Committee reviewed the resident’s concern and noted that appropriate 
signage is in place, including a WEEBLE. Hill confirmed no record of recent 
pedestrian accidents at the intersection. Demers agreed to upgrade the crosswalk 
signage that appeared to be faded. Hill will reach out to the resident to have the 
grass panel mowed. 
 
 e.  Resident request through SeeClickFix for a crosswalk on Broadway near Rollins Park 
   The Committee reviewed the resident’s request and discussed concerns with 
adding mid-block crosswalks on Broadway when a crosswalk at the main entrance 
already exists.  
 
 f.  Resident request through SeeClickFix for a No-U turn sign at the intersection of Fort 
Eddy Road and Fort Eddy Plaza 
The Committee reviewed the resident’s request. Hill mentioned Schedule VIII
October 20, 2026 
Page 5 of 5 
 
U-Turns Prohibited in Designated Places (see Section 17-4-6). She suggested that it 
appears this movement is restricted by ordinance but wanted to complete more 
research on the history before placing a sign.  
 
 g.  Resident request through SeeClickFix for a crosswalk on Abbott Road at Loon Ave 
The Committee reviewed the resident’s request and agreed a crosswalk could be 
considered in the future with the City’s annual paving program.  
 
 h.  Resident request through SeeClickFix for an additional sign on Little Pond Road 
prior to the stop control at Auburn Street 
The Committee reviewed the resident’s concerns and based on recent discussions 
regarding the intersection, agreed that adequate signage is in place. The 
Committee did not recommend further action at this time.  
 
 i.  Resident request through SeeClickFix for a crosswalk on Bow Street at Rockingham 
Street 
The Committee reviewed the resident’s concerns and confirmed crosswalks are 
not required at stop-controlled, minor intersection approaches. Based on the area 
and for consistency, the Committee did not recommend adding a crosswalk at this 
time.  
 
8.    Next Meeting 
November 17, 2026 
 
9.   Adjourn 
On a motion made by Palmer, seconded by Hill, the meeting adjourned at 10:52 
am. All in favor. 
    
Minutes prepared by Karen Hill and Sarah Ferguson
